analysis: The PR changes only documentation: docs/architecture/inference.md (head range 252-259, outside the supplied head excerpts but shown in the patch) and docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (a date bump and a new paragraph at head 784-790). No source, crypto, auth or wire-protocol code changed. The new text says a provider-staged complete-checkpoint import creates its destinations already available from host bytes and never evaluates or fences them. Staging therefore does not wait on MLX-Swift's process-wide evalLock, which the engine holds during another request's prefill chunk. The import plan also charges the largest host-zero source as staging scratch. This relates to T-041 (encrypted SSD prefix cache) and T-010 (availability), and describes an availability and latency improvement. Open question for later review: the code in CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift and the SSD staging path was not supplied. The review could not check that host-byte-backed destinations are still reached only after DBK3 AES-GCM authentication and the context and identity bindings. It also could not check that the host plaintext staging scratch is bounded, charged to the memory reservation and cleaned up. Host KV plaintext in RAM falls under existing T-011/T-014 operator-memory exposure, so there is no new trust-boundary change evident from docs alone. The T-041 text does not mention this staging path. Its transient-RAM description (one shared reservation per staged entry) may need a note if the scratch is outside that reservation. This is a coverage limit, not a finding. No security regression is claimed.
